summary: This note describes San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro, a Roman Catholic basilica and former cathedral of the Augustinians in Pavia, Lombardy, Italy. It explains the name, which refers to gold-leaf mosaics behind glass tesserae decorating the apse ceiling. It also notes the church's plain brick exterior with sandstone quoins and window framing, and that the floor now sits lower than the modern Piazza San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro in front of the façade.
one_line: San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro is an Augustinian basilica and former cathedral in Pavia, Italy, known for its gold-leaf apse mosaics.
key_facts: San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro is a Roman Catholic basilica and former cathedral of the Augustinians in Pavia, Italy.
The church is located in the Lombardy region of Italy.
The name San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro is Italian for "Saint Peter in Golden Sky".
The name refers to mosaics of gold leaf behind glass tesserae that decorate the ceiling of the apse.
The plain exterior of San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro is made of brick.
The exterior of San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro has sandstone quoins and window framing.
The paving of the San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro church floor is now lower than the modern street level of Piazza San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro.
Piazza San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro lies in front of the church's façade.
